title: The Joy of Earth Is Fleeting
description: The Joy of Earth Is Fleeting in Tonic Solfa to EWING, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Greek Office Books (Paisley, 1904).
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Sevens and Sixes Double (7.6.7.6.7.6.7.6), and this page sets them to EWING; any other Sevens and Sixes Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: The joy of earth is fleet-ing, The bliss of heaven re-mains; More sweet than earth-ly mu-sic The an-gel's glad re-frains; And hearts of saints up-ris-ing Find vent in sweet-est song, And lips of saints and an-gels The praise of heaven pro-long.

lines: The joy of earth is fleeting,
And lips of saints and angels
O Christ, who art for ever
With those whom Thou dost love,
The love that brought Thee earthward,
The love that stooped and died,
Be Thee our theme who linger
And teach our hearts to love Thee,
Our lips to praise Thee well;

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the Greek Office Books (1904)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the Greek Office Books; set to EWING by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
